headline: Reform UK vows to block the £5bn Peak Cluster carbon-capture scheme if elected
summary: Reform UK deputy leader Richard Tice, with the party's leaders of Staffordshire and Derbyshire county councils, wrote to Peak Cluster's private-sector backers warning it would block all planning applications for the proposed CO2 pipeline network — gathering emissions from Derbyshire and Staffordshire cement and lime plants for storage beneath the east Irish Sea — if the party enters government, branding it a 'net zero vanity project'.
co2crc_note: A national political party threatening to block a flagship UK CCS cluster is a live social-licence and political-risk signal — relevant to how Australian CCS projects (CarbonNet, Moomba) sustain community consent and bipartisan policy support.
extractor_note: Core of the item is political opposition, not a financial commitment; the £5bn is scheme cost and ~£30m is criticised National Wealth Fund backing, so amount left null per project-cost / non-commitment rules. Story dated 13 Sep UK = 14 Sep Melbourne, inside the Tuesday window; on-page date unverifiable (trade-press egress blocked), confirmed via Google-Alerts timestamp feed and multiple outlets.

headline: Community benefit fund launched for areas hosting HyNet's Liverpool Bay CO2 transport-and-storage infrastructure
summary: Liverpool Bay CCS Limited (Eni-operated) launched a voluntary Community Benefit Fund for Cheshire and Flintshire communities near the HyNet CO2 transport-and-storage network, funding local education, environmental and heritage projects around Liverpool Bay.
co2crc_note: Voluntary host-community benefit funds are a social-licence model CO2CRC can watch for Otway/CarbonNet community engagement.
extractor_note: Radar item — Chester Standard reported 'published 2 days ago' (~12 Sep), just outside the Tuesday 14-15 Sep Melbourne window; surfaced as Still-on-the-radar (<=7 days). No fund size disclosed, so amount null.
